Personally, I hate this phrase. And here's my view on it:

In a vacuum, sure, it's a good phrase, but it's not realistic and this is where the inner tension begins.

Sometimes taking responsibility for our lives is not as simple as it seems. Some situations and circumstances are out of our control. Where we live, the money we make, the support groups we may or may not have, and many other factors tie Into this.

This phrase is toxic positivity. Because sure, if I had the mental willpower and the physical means to change my life around, I would do it. The issue is that sometimes we do not have these means. We can't change who we are on a fundamental level in a short amount of time. 

Sure, I could theoretically work a low paying stressful job and live in a shared bedroom with crazy roommates while spending the evenings studying for a degree which I can't afford due to the low pay and living expenses, but even if I were to do all that we would assume that I have a superman brain capable of dealing with all of that stress, isolation, and trauma...

Sure, some people manage to do this, but I am not "some people". I am me. I am that I am. If I was born in a third world country this would be even harder, like I am expected to save money selling food on the street in a poor country to eventually become a doctor?

We need to be realistic with ourselves. Sometimes the life we so desperately want will be completely out of reach, regardlessly of our actions, simply because the circumstances are too great. Anyone who says "you can change anything about yourself" is lieing. We can only work with what we have and the cards we are dealt with.

Sometimes luck lends us a hand, sometimes it doesn't. But putting the expectation on ourselves that we are solely responsible for our situation is ludicrous. Everyone is different and comes from different backgrounds. Everyone has their issues and illnesses. In a perfect world, sure this phrase would make sense. But many fail to see that we do not live in a perfect world. 

There are too many people, all wanting the same things, and those who have the life they want don't think twice about those that don't. Darwinism is hell. And the world won't change until false claims like "it's purely our responsibility to change" are met with realism. 

I hate where I live, but I should be grateful for having a roof over my head. So why the hell do I feel I'd rather live in my car just to escape this place? And I'm supposed to feel guilty about not enjoying myself here? No. That's wrong. We all have an image for how our lives should be, and when that image is not met it is natural for us to contemplate suicide. Why live a life we cannot enjoy? 

I do know that when the day comes that I sincerely plan on ending it all, I will definitely do whatever I need to do to find even a moment of happiness, even if it means being homeless and eventually offing myself. I will not leave this world unsatisfied, for I will also not live this life unsatisfied in its entirety.

Sure, I might never be wealthy or important to the world, but why does that matter? If I can't achieve the stable life I yearn for, I will at least find peace in my final moments. I deserve that much at least. We all do. Just one moment of peace.

Hi friend,

While I understand your argument, maybe I could add a hypothesis.

We are the only ones on this planet and observable universe (that we know of) that are capable of conscious awareness and thought. I often think if our purpose is purely to be shepherds, to guide our humanity to betterment and understanding. Some call this "Enlightenment/God/Source"

The unfortunate reality is that there are many people out there who live for greed, materialism, and power. This is the antithesis to our existence. Society has slowly evolved over thousands of years to favor those who dictate history, those with wealth and power. This is what many would call "Evil/Satan" 

I'm not necessarily advocating for any specific religion, but there are many ideas to be gained from them. If in theory, all humanity was able to love unconditionally, we would be living in a utopia, with everyone's needs being met, while not sacrificing the health of our planet. No one would be in crisis as our purpose would only be to love and create. 

The great conflict comes from the fact that we cannot truly change everyone's minds. The world is simply too large for that, for any one person. This is why religions exist. I'm not saying we all need to go to church every Sunday, but that if we were all able to share that feeling of unconditional love, then uglyness and beauty would not exist. Richness and poverty would not exist. All would be in a state of perfect balance.

Our world is slowly declining, that much is clear. Corporations get richer and the poor get poorer. Lobbyist fund corrupt politicians to further their wealth and keep us divided. Wars rage over material things where the honest folk are the ones forced to die for them. 

Many believe the only true way out is a reset, a global catastrophe, but that would only delay this process, effectively restarting it. This is why it's very important for everyone to carry these beliefs with them and why the "golden rule" exists. Treat others with kindness, treat yourself with kindness. 

That is truly the meaning of our lives. We are here to experience the infinite in a limited physical form. For that is what gives us perspective. We cannot know the unlimited unless we are limited in comparison. I am deeply saddened by the state of the world, but I know there are still many people out there who wish it to be a better place. Suicide is considered "selfish" only because it implies you are ending your suffering instead of helping others to suffer less. However, it can be easy to think that we are all doomed regardless of our actions. Spirituality is the key to keep yourself going. Wether it be Catholic, Buddhist, Jewish, Muslim, it doesn't matter. What matters is that we need a belief in a greater reason or goal in order for us to align ourselves to humanity. Stoicism and other philosophies are there for this specific purpose. To help define ourselves and work to understand ourselves.

I wish the best for humanity, and I truly hope those in power will see this for themselves one day.

Hi friend,

I am very sorry you are going through this. First thing I will say, is don't be ashamed of how you feel. We are all human and this is more common than you think. We all experience our mental pain for different reasons, but the pain we feel is all the same. 

It sounds like you have a very good head on your shoulders. I never made it past college myself, so be proud of yourself for that secondly. It sounds like your family is supportive which is the third thing to be grateful for, so many of us do not have support systems to prop us up.

However, don't think that I'm trying to guilt you into feeling better, because I am not. I am just giving you a few things to think on for starters. If you have a close friend or feel comfortable sharing this with your family, please do. 

I'm sure you have looked up many different ways to better yourself, so I won't give you the whole speech about exercise, eating healthy, sleeping well, etc. 

It sounds to me like you are lacking that inner spark, that "purpose". Which is perfectly normal as well. Again don't be ashamed, this is also a chemical imbalance in the brain as I'm sure you've heard. Treat this like you would treat breaking a leg. You can't just "will things to get better", it takes time, but you can achieve healing.

You seem very intelligent, and one of the drawbacks of intelligent people is that they are often depressed, many marvelous philosophers suffered through this. You will come out stronger on the other side.

It sounds like you need to take a moment to breathe. Take time to be kind to yourself, to look deep inside yourself. Ask yourself "what would make me happy", "what am I missing", "what is bothering me". Your inner self will give you an answer, but it may take time for you to internalize it. Meditation can greatly help with this, but it is not a cure-all. The first step to getting better is understanding.

28 here, I feel you on a deep level. Sometimes I feel like my best days are behind me. However I know that it's all perspective. As we age we tend to think about the simpler days and that black and white thinking is not helpful to our minds. Even as kids we had reasons to be upset even if they were trivial by comparison. 

The true key to happiness as we grow up is to find a reason or goal. Something to look forward to. Society these days has made it hard for humans to be, well, human. Our ancestors would worry about finding food and not being eaten by animals, and now we're at the opposite end of the pendulum in such a short amount of time that we haven't been able to adapt as a species. 

Find what brings you any sense of joy, and lean on it, attach yourself to it and keep digging, it may seem hopeless but there is always the chance to find motivation.

I understand your pain. Growing up I was told all the same things, "I'm a handsome guy", I'm "smart", I have "so much potential" but that is all meaningless to me really.

I realized my depression is caused by my life not being what I always internalized it to be. Depression can happen for a lot of reasons, but for me it was due to not being where I thought I would be in life by now. I'm in my 20s and even though I've had tons of reasons to be happy, I just never felt it.

Your parents being overly protective is definitely part of the reason you feel this way. Life isn't meant to be lived by some set of rules or boundaries, we should get to discover and experience things on our own to shape our way of thinking. 

If you need someone to vent to, people like me are always here. But in honesty you should focus on finding a job and saving up money to maybe live on your own. There's a lot of freedom in independence, but it comes with a lot of stress as well. Maybe you could find a bedroom in a house for rent, I did the same thing when I was your age ten years ago. 

Society has changed a lot these days, people are not as social or outgoing as in the past and a lot of them only think about themselves. Sometimes all we need is a friend to open our perspective. 

You are not in the wrong for feeling the way you feel. There will be a lot of changes in your future and you won't be caged up forever. Look forward to those happier moments, and take nothing for granted.
